explanation_en: This set phrase is used to indicate that something happens very quickly or within a very short limit of time. It is followed by a noun phrase denoting time or quantity (e.g., 'en cuestión de segundos', 'en cuestión de días'). It is a standard, highly useful formula in both colloquial and formal registers.

examples.en_text: The plumber solved the pipe problem in a matter of minutes.
examples.target_text: El fontanero solucionó el problema de la tubería en cuestión de minutos.

examples.en_text: The new product sold out in a matter of days after its launch.
examples.target_text: El nuevo producto se agotó en cuestión de días tras su lanzamiento.

examples.en_text: The weather changed completely in a matter of hours; we went from sunshine to rain.
examples.target_text: El clima cambió por completo en cuestión de horas; pasamos del sol a la lluvia.

examples.en_text: With this new connection, you can download the movie in a matter of seconds.
examples.target_text: Con esta nueva conexión, puedes descargar la película en cuestión de segundos.

examples.en_text: She learned to use the design program in a matter of weeks thanks to the tutorials.
examples.target_text: Aprendió a usar el programa de diseño en cuestión de semanas gracias a los tutoriales.

examples.en_text: If there is no traffic, we can get to the airport in a matter of half an hour.
examples.target_text: Si no hay tráfico, podemos llegar al aeropuerto en cuestión de media hora.

explanation_en: This is an idiomatic expression meaning to be left completely shocked, devastated, or empty inside due to a tragic event. It conveys a deep emotional impact, similar to 'having one's heart sink' or 'being left breathless'. It is highly expressive and used in dramatic or deeply moving contexts.

examples.en_text: When she told me she didn't love me anymore, I was left devastated.
examples.target_text: Cuando ella me dijo que ya no me quería, me quedé sin alma.

examples.en_text: After seeing the fire, the neighbors were left devastated upon seeing their destroyed houses.
examples.target_text: Después de ver el incendio, los vecinos se quedaron sin alma al ver sus casas destruidas.

examples.en_text: Juan was left devastated when he found out he had lost his lifelong job.
examples.target_text: Juan se quedó sin alma cuando se enteró de que había perdido su trabajo de toda la vida.

examples.en_text: If we were to lose the championship in the last minute, we would be left devastated.
examples.target_text: Si perdiéramos el campeonato en el último minuto, nos quedaríamos sin alma.

examples.en_text: Have you been left devastated after hearing that sad news? I notice you are very quiet.
examples.target_text: ¿Te has quedado sin alma tras escuchar esa triste noticia? Te noto muy callado.

examples.en_text: It is impossible not to be left devastated when reading about the consequences of war.
examples.target_text: Es imposible no quedarse sin alma al leer sobre las consecuencias de la guerra.

explanation_en: This is a discourse marker used to summarize or conclude a point, translating to 'ultimately', 'in short', or 'all in all'. It is extremely common in both spoken and written Spanish to wrap up an argument or a list of descriptions. It helps structure speech naturally.

examples.en_text: We can buy the blue car or the red one, but, ultimately, you are the one who is going to drive it.
examples.target_text: Podemos comprar el coche azul o el rojo, pero, en definitiva, tú eres quien va a conducirlo.

examples.en_text: There were many problems during the project, but, in the end, we managed to finish it on time.
examples.target_text: Hubo muchos problemas durante el proyecto, pero, en definitiva, logramos terminarlo a tiempo.

examples.en_text: It doesn't matter what others say; ultimately, the only thing that counts is your happiness.
examples.target_text: No importa lo que digan los demás; en definitiva, lo único que cuenta es tu felicidad.

examples.en_text: We wanted to go to the beach, but the weather was bad, so, ultimately, we stayed at home.
examples.target_text: Queríamos ir a la playa, pero el clima era malo, así que, en definitiva, nos quedamos en casa.

examples.en_text: The new director changed some rules, but, ultimately, the company's strategy remains the same.
examples.target_text: El nuevo director cambió algunas normas, pero, en definitiva, la estrategia de la empresa sigue siendo la misma.

examples.en_text: You can do many diets, but, ultimately, the most important thing is to eat a balanced diet.
examples.target_text: Puedes hacer muchas dietas, pero, en definitiva, lo más importante es comer de forma equilibrada.

explanation_en: This is a very common colloquial idiom meaning to take a quick swim or dip in the water (pool, beach, river). It is the standard informal way to talk about going for a quick, refreshing swim, especially during hot weather.

examples.en_text: It's a very hot day, why don't we take a quick dip in the sea?
examples.target_text: Hace un día muy caluroso, ¿por qué no nos damos un chapuzón en el mar?

examples.en_text: After running through the park, I just want to get home and take a quick dip in the pool.
examples.target_text: Después de correr por el parque, solo quiero llegar a casa y darme un chapuzón en la piscina.

examples.en_text: Yesterday we went hiking to the lake and took a quick dip before eating.
examples.target_text: Ayer fuimos de excursión al lago y nos dimos un chapuzón rápido antes de comer.

examples.en_text: If the water weren't so cold, I would take a quick dip right now.
examples.target_text: Si el agua no estuviera tan fría, me daría un chapuzón ahora mismo.

examples.en_text: Come on, take off your shirt and take a quick dip with us! The water is great.
examples.target_text: ¡Venga, quítate la camiseta y date un chapuzón con nosotros! El agua está buenísima.

examples.en_text: While the kids were taking a quick dip, the parents were preparing the food in the garden.
examples.target_text: Mientras los niños se daban un chapuzón, los padres preparaban la comida en el jardín.

explanation_en: This is a fixed adverbial locution meaning 'door to door'. It is used to describe actions like campaigning, selling, or in this case, warning residents individually by visiting each house. It is simple but highly idiomatic and preferred over 'de casa en casa' in many contexts.

examples.en_text: The encyclopedia salesman used to go door to door in our neighborhood.
examples.target_text: El vendedor de enciclopedias iba puerta por puerta en nuestro barrio.

examples.en_text: We looked for our lost cat by asking door to door along the whole street.
examples.target_text: Buscamos a nuestro gato perdido preguntando puerta por puerta en toda la calle.

examples.en_text: The campaign volunteers went door to door to talk to the neighbors.
examples.target_text: Los voluntarios de la campaña electoral pasaron puerta por puerta para hablar con los vecinos.

examples.en_text: A group of students is going door to door to do a survey about recycling.
examples.target_text: Un grupo de estudiantes está yendo puerta por puerta para hacer una encuesta sobre el reciclaje.

examples.en_text: Last week, the Red Cross went door to door asking for donations.
examples.target_text: La semana pasada, la Cruz Roja pasó puerta por puerta pidiendo donaciones.

examples.en_text: The police went door to door warning people about the storm.
examples.target_text: La policía fue puerta por puerta advirtiendo a la gente sobre la tormenta.

explanation_en: The construction 'nada más + infinitive' is a very common and natural way to say 'as soon as [action happens]' or 'immediately upon [doing something]'. It is highly preferred in spoken Spanish over 'tan pronto como' or 'en cuanto'. It is a key structure for B2/C1 learners to master for fluid storytelling.

examples.en_text: As soon as I got home, I took off my shoes and sat on the sofa.
examples.target_text: Nada más llegar a casa, me quité los zapatos y me senté en el sofá.

examples.en_text: As soon as he arrived at the office, the boss called him for an urgent meeting.
examples.target_text: Nada más llegar a la oficina, el jefe lo llamó para una reunión urgente.

examples.en_text: As soon as we arrived at the hotel, we went straight to the pool.
examples.target_text: Nada más llegar al hotel, fuimos directamente a la piscina.

examples.en_text: As soon as you arrive at the station, call me so I can go pick you up.
examples.target_text: Nada más llegar a la estación, llámame para que vaya a buscarte.

examples.en_text: As soon as they arrived at the party, they realized they had gotten the day wrong.
examples.target_text: Nada más llegar a la fiesta, se dieron cuenta de que se habían equivocado de día.

examples.en_text: As soon as I arrive in Madrid, I want to go eat some good churros.
examples.target_text: Nada más llegar a Madrid, quiero ir a comer unos buenos churros.

explanation_en: This verbal collocation means to carry out, execute, or lead a project, protest, or initiative. It is extremely common in both formal and informal contexts, such as business, politics, and social movements, instead of just using 'hacer' or 'realizar'.

examples.en_text: We are carrying out a very important project for the company.
examples.target_text: Estamos llevando adelante un proyecto muy importante para la empresa.

examples.en_text: Despite the difficulties, she managed to push forward with her own business.
examples.target_text: A pesar de las dificultades, ella logró llevar adelante su propio negocio.

examples.en_text: The government is carrying out new educational reforms.
examples.target_text: El gobierno está llevando adelante nuevas reformas educativas.

examples.en_text: We need a good leader to carry out this plan.
examples.target_text: Necesitamos un buen líder para llevar adelante este plan.

examples.en_text: They carried out the investigation without the help of the police.
examples.target_text: Ellos llevaron adelante la investigación sin la ayuda de la policía.

examples.en_text: How do you plan to carry out this proposal without a budget?
examples.target_text: ¿Cómo piensas llevar adelante esta propuesta sin presupuesto?

explanation_en: This idiomatic phrase is used to emphatically state that something never happened or was never the case. It is much stronger and more formal than simply saying 'nunca' or 'jamás'. It is frequently used in debates, legal contexts, and formal arguments to deny accusations.

examples.en_text: At no point did I want to offend you, it was just an opinion.
examples.target_text: En ningún momento quise ofenderte, solo era una opinión.

examples.en_text: She assured me that at no point did she think about leaving the project.
examples.target_text: Ella me aseguró que en ningún momento pensó en dejar el proyecto.

examples.en_text: During the trip, at no point did we feel unsafe.
examples.target_text: Durante el viaje, en ningún momento nos sentimos inseguros.

examples.en_text: The suspect denied the accusations and said that at no point was he there.
examples.target_text: El sospechoso negó las acusaciones y dijo que en ningún momento estuvo allí.

examples.en_text: My phone was connected to the Wi-Fi, but at no point did the video load.
examples.target_text: Mi teléfono estaba conectado al wifi, pero en ningún momento se cargó el video.

examples.en_text: The exam was difficult, but at no point did I lose hope of passing.
examples.target_text: El examen era difícil, pero en ningún momento perdí la esperanza de aprobar.

explanation_en: This highly common colloquial idiom means that something happened suddenly, unexpectedly, or without any apparent cause. It is equivalent to 'out of the blue' or 'out of thin air' in English. It is widely used in everyday conversations across all Spanish-speaking countries.

examples.en_text: Out of nowhere, it started to rain very hard and we had to look for shelter.
examples.target_text: De la nada, empezó a llover muy fuerte y tuvimos que buscar refugio.

examples.en_text: She stopped talking to me out of the blue and I still don't know why.
examples.target_text: Ella dejó de hablarme de la nada y todavía no sé por qué.

examples.en_text: That singer became famous out of nowhere thanks to a viral video.
examples.target_text: Ese cantante se hizo famoso de la nada gracias a un video viral.

examples.en_text: A dog appeared out of nowhere in the middle of the road and I had to brake.
examples.target_text: Un perro apareció de la nada en medio de la carretera y tuve que frenar.

examples.en_text: My head started to hurt out of the blue while I was working.
examples.target_text: Me empezó a doler la cabeza de la nada mientras estaba trabajando.

examples.en_text: The solution to the problem came to me out of nowhere when I was having a coffee.
examples.target_text: La solución al problema se me ocurrió de la nada cuando estaba tomando un café.

explanation_en: This is a colloquial adverbial phrase particularly common in Rioplatense Spanish (Argentina and Uruguay) meaning 'perfectly fine', 'very well', or 'without any issues'. While standard Spanish would use 'muy bien' or 'perfectamente', 'lo más bien' adds a native, informal flavor to describe a state or action that was going smoothly.

examples.en_text: Yesterday I had a headache, but today I already feel perfectly fine.
examples.target_text: Ayer me dolía la cabeza, pero hoy ya me siento lo más bien.

examples.en_text: Don't worry about the computer, it's already working perfectly fine.
examples.target_text: No te preocupes por la computadora, ya funciona lo más bien.

examples.en_text: The trip was a bit long, but we arrived at the hotel perfectly fine.
examples.target_text: El viaje fue un poco largo, pero llegamos lo más bien al hotel.

examples.en_text: I thought the exam would be difficult, but I passed it perfectly fine.
examples.target_text: Pensé que el examen sería difícil, pero lo aprobé lo más bien.

examples.en_text: My parents get along perfectly well with my in-laws.
examples.target_text: Mis parents se llevan lo más bien con mis suegros.

examples.en_text: We live perfectly fine in this apartment, even though it's a bit small.
examples.target_text: Vivimos lo más bien en este departamento, aunque sea un poco chico.

explanation_en: This versatile pronominal verb means to take responsibility for something, to take charge of a situation, or to own up to an action. In Argentina and other regions, it can also mean to feel targeted by a comment or to accept a reality. It is a crucial B2/C1 expression for discussing accountability.

examples.en_text: We will take care of the problem, don't worry.
examples.target_text: Nosotros nos hacemos cargo del problema, no te preocupes.

examples.en_text: I'll take care of the travel expenses.
examples.target_text: Yo me hago cargo de los gastos del viaje.

examples.en_text: They took charge of the office while the boss was on vacation.
examples.target_text: Ellos se hicieron cargo de la oficina mientras el jefe estaba de vacaciones.

examples.en_text: Who is going to take charge of organizing tomorrow's meeting?
examples.target_text: ¿Quién se va a hacer cargo de organizar la reunión de mañana?

examples.en_text: If you can't, we will take care of watching the kids this afternoon.
examples.target_text: Si tú no puedes, nosotros nos hacemos cargo de cuidar a los niños esta tarde.

examples.en_text: You are an adult now, it's time for you to take responsibility for your own decisions.
examples.target_text: Ya eres adulto, es hora de que te hagas cargo de tus propias decisiones.

explanation_en: This collocation is widely used in social, political, and journalistic contexts to mean bringing attention to a cause, issue, or marginalized group. Instead of using 'mostrar' (to show), 'hacer visible' implies a conscious effort to raise awareness or expose something that was previously ignored or hidden.

examples.en_text: This campaign seeks to make the issue of mental health in young people visible.
examples.target_text: Esta campaña busca hacer visible el problema de la salud mental en los jóvenes.

examples.en_text: It is important to make your work visible so that the bosses recognize your effort.
examples.target_text: Es importante hacer visible tu trabajo para que los jefes reconozcan tu esfuerzo.

examples.en_text: The application's new update makes visible the options that were previously hidden.
examples.target_text: La nueva actualización de la aplicación hace visibles las opciones que antes estaban ocultas.

examples.en_text: The teacher used real-life examples to make such an abstract concept visible.
examples.target_text: El profesor usó ejemplos de la vida real para hacer visible un concepto tan abstracto.

examples.en_text: Through his photos, the artist wants to make the beauty of everyday things visible.
examples.target_text: A través de sus fotos, el artista quiere hacer visible la belleza de las cosas cotidianas.

examples.en_text: Yesterday's protest managed to make the neighbors' discontent visible.
examples.target_text: La protesta de ayer logró hacer visible el descontento de los vecinos.
